Amapanyaza

By: Bongani Bingwa | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are Gauteng's new Crime Prevention Wardens the Premier's illegal private army?

Unique Selling Point:
Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi says his 6000 newly employed officers are still in training as they wait the gazetting of their duties by various departments. So why have they been deployed to various crime hotspots around the province? On what basis did they allegedly assault "Sipho" who sustained extensive injuries that have left him barely able to walk and reliant on a catheter to urinate? If not yet properly constituted, how is this force being paid? By what authority? Is the money allocated to them being used properly? "Sipho" will share his dramatic assault by these wardens and how it has nearly destroyed his life.

Summary:
Hastily trained over s few weeks, questions have been raised about the wide-ranging powers the AmaPanyaza have to fight crime. The province calls them "peace officers" but were they constituted properly under the law? The justice ministry says they did not gazette this as required in legislation. Since they have hit the streets allegations have emerged that they have beaten residents of Ekurhuleni including a young man who has been left unable to urinate on his own and uses a catheter. The wider question is also about the money and whether funds were diverted from NGOs looking after the elderly and disabled to create this unit.

Expert:
Mr. Gareth Newham ISS Head of Criminal Justice
Mr. Panyaza Lesufi
Mr. Ronald Lamola

Press Release:


30 year old Andrew Make does not feel lucky to be alive. Until a few weeks ago, he spent his nights in unendurable agony as a result of injuries he sustained in a beating, allegedly not from criminals but rather Gauteng’s new crime busters, Amapanyaza. They forced their way into his home on a midmorning week demanding to search the property for illicit drugs. When they found none, he challenged them and that is when he says the beating started. His is just one of a number of allegations against the Crime Prevention Wardens. Hastily trained, how well equipped are they to keep the streets of Gauteng safe?

Script:


Amapanyaza

Intro

Commentary One
Crime in South Africa is out of control. Gauteng, the COUNTRY’S economic hub is plagued by violent incidents.

Commentary Two
Our murder rate now is around 46, 47 murders per 100,000 compared to the global average of six murders, 100,000,

MARK HEYWOOD
Between April and June this year, there were 1489 murders. There were, I think, nearly 10,000 rapes. There were 7000 robberies.

Commentary Three
But the Gauteng’s premier, Panyaza Lesufi has a plan…

PANYAZA LESUFI
“6000 young people have been recruited to go to training so that they can be combat ready to patrol our communities… these young people will invade all our street in Gauteng from the 1st of May 2023… this is a strong message to criminals – we are ready to confront you, wherever you are.

ANDREW
I was not a criminal. I didn't commit any crime, but I was treated like a criminal.
_______________________

Act One

LINK
11 Diagonal Street. Once the seat of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the hub of the city's financial district. But that was a long time ago. Many businesses have left because of crime. Well not under my watch, says this premier.

Commentary Four
At the State of the Province address in February, he unveiled a bold initiative.

PANYAZA LESUFI
The issue of fighting crime should be our apex priority. We are increasing the budget of fighting crime from R750m to multi billion rands in the next three years


Commentary Five
And so, Premier Lesufi launched the Crime Prevention Wardens, taking to social media to advertise 6000 posts.

Within weeks he was ready to unveil his cadets.

PANYAZA LESUFI
I can see now that you are fit and proper. I’m releasing you to each and every township. Those that don’t respect you, they will regret! Phezukwabo (Get on top of them!)”

Commentary Six
But as soon as they hit the ground there were problems.

MARK HEYWOOD
I think I was the first person to really kind of start to dig deep and look into the systems and the policies and and so on around this initiative..

Commentary Seven
Mark Heywood is the Editor of the on-line publication Maverick Citizen. He received a call from a desperate mother who alleged her son had been assaulted.
MARK HEYWOOD
There had been some stuff in the media, of course. There had been allegations that there were already some questions about the training, whether the training was adequate - there was an allegation they had been involved in the murder of an alleged drug dealer which had been denied.

Commentary Eight
30 year old call center agent Andrew Make, says it was the crime wardens.

ANDREW MAKE
I heard a commotion happening that was happening outside. So I opened my door. I saw a bunch of guys in like these green overalls and berets on and and the ski masks.
_______________________

Act Two

LINK
Andrew was at home lying on his bed. It was mid-morning in the middle of the week. He's off day. He was resting. He had no idea how his life was about to change.




ANDREW MAKE
They then came to my door and then they said they would also like to search in my room as well because they received information that there's someone on this property that is selling drugs to schoolchildren and so forth.

Before they even began their search. I declared that I have my own cannabis. I showed it to them. It was in like a small peanut butter jar. I said, This is what I use on my personal use. Other than that, you can you may go ahead and search the room.

They went in like to my bags and my clothing as well. They threw everything onto the floor. Some of them were shouting from the outside that they should check in the inside the grocery, So that's when they started throwing out like my mealy meal. My, my, my, my rice. My macaroni was thrown out on the floor.

Commentary Nine
But that was only the start of his ordeal - a week later, they were back. But this time he demanded a search warrant

ANDREW MAKE
That's when most of them went ballistic. They said, obviously there must be something that you hiding if you don't want us to search. We're going search even if we have to forcibly come in.

Commentary Ten
And that is when Andrew says thing took a turn for the worst. After ransacking his room once more, they demanded his small jar of cannabis. He refused

ANDREW MAKE

One of them picked me up and threw me against the wall and it was just an onslaught of abuse at that moment. I was on the floor covering my head like this. I could feel boots hitting my ribs, knocks coming to my head. Some of them kicked me in my groin area, in my bum area,

You were thinking smart to put or you think you're clever. I'm just screaming. Stop, stop, Please stop

Commentary Eleven
When they stopped, the first thing Andrew did was to call his mother. She was shocked when she got to him.

CAROLINE MAKE
00:06:40:32 - 00:07:04:35
He was like half dead animal the way he was. He was like, It's not my son. I know. Just lying dead, doing nothing. And then I see what what I did. Why did what made him to do this to you? They almost killed my son.

Commentary
Andrew sustained such severe injuries he now relies on a catheter to urinate and is still undergoing extensive urology treatment
_______________________

Act Three

Commentary Twelve
This hardly surprised Mandla Nyaqela, a former Crime Prevention Warden.

MANDLA NYAQELA
No, I was not surprised to hear that these guys were beating up members of the public because some of the trainers were former correctional service officials. And you can imagine, you know, someone who was a correctional service official who dealt with inmates. There was this notion that they needed to get out us a soft man and put in a strong man who is going to combat against crime and criminals.

It felt like we've just been trained for brutalism, you know.


LINK
Fighting crime is the Premier's apex priority, he says. But are hit 6000 crime prevention wardens preventing crime or creating it.

Commentary Thirteen
The Gauteng Premier’s spokesperson, Sizwe Pamla is aware of Andrew’s allegations.

SIZWE PAMLA
There is currently an investigation that is taking place with regard to the allegations that emanate from Katlehong, where it is alleged that in the course of doing their work, they manhandled, allegedly manhandled a citizen there.

Commentary Fourteen
But Sizwe argues crime fighting is serious business

SIZWE PAMLA
These people, police in townships, informal settlements, hostels. These are some of the most violent areas in this province.

During training of any law enforcement unit there are people who quit because once they realize what is it that is going to confront them on the streets that they say, I am not ready for this.



Commentary Fifteen
Mandla is a member of a Community Police Forum.. He says he joined Amapanyaza with high expectations but eventually quit.

MANDLA
We did aerobics. We didn't push ups, sit ups; We, we, we ran around the camp. Um, yeah, basically nothing else. And we, they taught us drills also, left, right, left .

Commentary Sixteen
Police searches are conducted under strict regulations - at the very least officers must identify themselves. So why do so many allege these wardens cover their faces?

SIZWE PAMLA
00:16:37:35 - 00:17:06:05
No, that's actually not true

This is not some vigilante militia that is operating outside of the law. That uniform is inspected by SAPS; as in when they walk in for duty, they come in and they undergo inspections. Whatever a mask that they wear, they wear it nine out of ten at night because of cold

Commentary Seventeen
Mandla has an entirely different reason

MANDLA
00:15:12:30 - 00:15:26:12
Many of these crime prevention wardens, officers are members of the same community that they go in to raid. They leave drug dealers, houses, they the raid shebeens and all of that. So I think they hide their faces just to protect their identity

BONGANI BINGWA
00:39:28:37 - 00:39:43:40
At the parade where these cadets were unveiled, some of them were holding guns and rifles. That seems an odd thing for people who are going to be going and doing essentially support services in community policing

SIZWE PAMLA
00:39:44:38 - 00:39:51:37
When you are policing a volatile province, you are not going to send people with batons to fight criminals

BONGANI BINGWA
00:39:52:01 - 00:39:52:49
With rifles, though?

SIZWE PAMLA
00:39:53:24 - 00:40:26:00
Yes, what do we expect crime wardens to bring into a fight where AK 47 are being welded up out on the streets they don't know is unacceptable. People should not pretend as if they have no appreciation of what crime levels look like in this country just because they're discussing crime wardens.

LINK
Clever explanations, ready answers. But what is accountable government, if not the ability to hear the most vulnerable? Those who've been abused who say to you something happened here that shouldn't have happened.

MARK HEYWOOD
00:16:04:07 - 00:16:22:35
He doesn't have justice. I mean, he's suffered terrible pain. He has had his body badly, badly damaged. He hasn't been able to urinate for two and a half months. I've had him on the phone in tears. I've had his mum on the phone in tears, devastated. He's lost his job. He has been suicidal. I mean, he has contemplated suicide on instances

CAROLINE MAKE
00:09:15:34 - 00:09:20:26
It's not fair. It's not fair. It's not fair.


BONGANI BINGWA
00:13:22:02 - 00:13:33:12
Mama, how does it feel to look at your son with this? With this bag?

CAROLINE MAKE
00:13:33:12 - 00:13:56:02
Right now. He doesn't see himself as a man. He doesn't see himself as a man he think is that. I don't know. And then also with this things. You think I'm going to get my grandchildren? No, I don't think so. The way they beat him, I don't think so.

BONGANI BINGWA
00:18:15:42 - 00:18:18:15
I'm sorry this happened to you.

CAROLINE MAKE

0:15:40:29 - 00:16:07:46
Been there apart. It was better than this apart. It I never been beaten by none. None of my family was beaten in apartheid…

___________________________________________________________

“We are sending you to patrol the townships…”

LINK

“These are the forgotten communities…”

V/O

Are Amapanyaza protectors or predators? We investigate allegations of abuse

PROMO TWO
Caroline UPS
“No-one has a right to hit anybody…”

V/O

They were meant to protect the streets but are Gauteng residents any safer?

PROMO THREE

When you are policing a volatile province, you are not going to send people with batons to fight criminals

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Are Gauteng's new Crime Prevention Wardens the Premier's illegal private army?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi says his 6000 newly employed officers are still in training as they wait the gazetting of their duties by various departments. So why have they been deployed to various crime hotspots around the province? On what basis did they allegedly assault "Sipho" who sustained extensive injuries that have left him barely able to walk and reliant on a catheter to urinate? If not yet properly constituted, how is this force being paid? By what authority? Is the money allocated to them being used properly? "Sipho" will share his dramatic assault by these wardens and how it has nearly destroyed his life.
metadata.Summary: Hastily trained over s few weeks, questions have been raised about the wide-ranging powers the AmaPanyaza have to fight crime. The province calls them "peace officers" but were they constituted properly under the law? The justice ministry says they did not gazette this as required in legislation. Since they have hit the streets allegations have emerged that they have beaten residents of Ekurhuleni including a young man who has been left unable to urinate on his own and uses a catheter. The wider question is also about the money and whether funds were diverted from NGOs looking after the elderly and disabled to create this unit.
